item.content:encoded:
("prodding" the car during manifestations and exploring the strip dimension)

How does this work?

At one point, a GoI destroys it with a rocket launcher.

What? This comes out of nowhere and seems too convenient of a plot device… unless this anomaly has something to do with this GoI (which you have not named, so I assume its not an integral part of the story) then it really doesn't make sense.

I am not feeling this idea, mostly because I think the phantom char thing is so overdone in media.

You could potentially make this more interesting with some characterization but without that, this will just be an article about ghost cars and the foundation's research into them… which doesn't do it for me.

I suggest thinking about how you could make this a character driven story, with someone for the reader to relate to. And think about the arc, where do we start vs where do we end, in terms of the narrative?

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

SCP-XXXX is to be stored in Containment Area M21 located in 300m underground of the Gobi desert in Mongolia.

Delete that second “in” (right before 300m)

SCP-XXXX is to be held in a 5 m cube made of entirely Tungsten metal, with no gap for organic life to enter.

Why does it matter that the cube be Five meters in length/widtch/height? What if it were 4.98 meters? Would that invalidate the containment? This is why specific measurements of containment chambers is mostly avoided these days.

If any entities that reside in SCP-XXXX-1 move from their position, they are to be immediately apprehended and interrogated before being held in a cell with same containment procedure as SCP-CXXX.

Suggest: Entities residing in SCP-XXXX-1 that move from their position, are to be apprehended, interrogated, and remanded to a containment cell under equivalent containment procedures as SCP-XXXX.

No more than five personnel wearing Hazmat suits, are to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at the same time. Its activity is to be monitored 24/7 and no unauthorized personnel and civilian are to be in the proximity of the area or enter SCP-XXXX-1.

Suggest: A maximum of five hazmat protected personnel are permitted to enter SCP-XXXX-1 at any given time. Access to SCP-XXXX-1 is restricted to security cleared personnel.

In the event of a Containment Breach, all on site researchers and personnel are to evacuate immediately or stay in shelter until the MTF Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) arrive at the facility and apprehended the entity.

Suggest: In the event of a containment breach, all on-site personnel are to evacuate or shelter in place until such time as MTF-Theta-4 (“Gardeners”) apprehend the entity.

ALSO: which entity? Clarify

SCP-CXXX consists of two components: a cave (SCP-XXXX-1) and humanoid protecting it (SCP-XXXX).

Suggest: SCP-XXXX consists of two interrelated anomalies: a cave, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 and a humanoid entity guarding the cave, designated as SCP-XXXX.
ALSO: I suggest reversing the designations, the Cave could be the XXXX and the humanoid, -1, because it seems the cave is the central anomaly.

SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sunburn and wears an old dark green Hun area deel1 which been ripped and torn, however, SCP-XXXX refused to change it.

SCP-XXXX has the ability to manifest entities made out of natural components which resemble a Chinese dragon. Entities length is unknown.
So several things, “an old dark green Hun area deel” is confusing… suggest: “SCP-XXXX is a Hun male, its skin is olive-brown from sun damage and an deteriorating, dark-green Hun deel that the entity refuses to change.” & I don’t know what “made out of natural components” means in this context, so I would clarify.

ALSO: IS this meant to be two paragraphs? If so, there is no spacing between them.

SCP-XXXX-1 is a cave under abandoned Mining factory, it is measured to be around 6 kilometers deep.

Suggest: a cave under an abandoned mining facility, measured to be approximately six kilometers below the surface.

  • There is no such thing as a mining factory, change this everywhere… it’s a facility or just a mine.

However, how big SCP-XXXX-1 mass is impossible to measure. SCP-XXXX-1 resides a snake-like creature approximately 1 kilometers, maybe even bigger.

Suggest: Exact measurements of SCP-XXXX-1’s dimensions have been impossible due to a large serpentine entity, at least one kilometer in length, that resides within the cave.

About fifty kilometers down, there is a massive field stretching further from the human eye, filled with stationary humanoids varies in ages, they're made out of natural components, different species of flowers but growing in the same root. The radio cuts off the moment entering SCP-XXXX-1.

Fifty kilometers down where? I thought you said the cave was 6 km below the surface? What do you mean? Also this is just really awkwardly written.

The investigation into SCP-XXXX-1 and its relation with SCP-XXXX is ongoing.

Cut this. It’s implied because there’s more to read after it.

This is a critique in progress… You have so many awkward phrases and poorly structured sentences… I would sit down and really examine your work here, and see if you can't clean it up without myself or another critter to do so.

Additionally, all the dialogue is stilted and hard to read. Go through it and say each line aloud, then if it sounds awkward try to make it sound more grounded and believable.

item.title: SCP Idea: Stuck in the Past
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a set of three anomalous access dial-up Internet access numbers, each with the same anomalous property: when you connect to it, your web browser is pretty much transported back to the late 2000s. Everything is as it was back then: web sites, web services, social media are all unchanged from their original forms back then, and it can all be interacted with by users of this SCP. For all intents and purposes, this SCP is a type of time machine.

Central Narrative: The Foundation discovers the existence of this SCP in 2017, and a few years later they use it to interview some people from the past. Through these interviews, they discover the possible origin of the SCP, and eventually they find one of its' creators. He explains how it was made and why it was made (making reference to an unnamed made-up SCP with time and reality manipulation powers which the foundation has not yet contained, cuz im too lazy to find an existing SCP matching those criteria :P)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There are many internet-based SCPs, but I have yet to see one which is directly affiliated with the internet itself rather than just using it as a medium through which to do its "thing". The internet is a big and scary place, and I feel like its many different subcultures and groups (and its history) have so much potential as a source of inspiration for SCPs. After all, without the internet, the Foundation wouldn't exist ;)

Additional Notes: I've already typed up a draft of the entire article + the chat/interview logs, if you want me to post it here I can.

Thanks for reading my idea, everyone! This is my second real SCP idea that I've posted here, and it's the first one that I'm really, truly super proud of ^u^ It's been such a long time, I honestly forgot how much I love writing…

item.title: Re: A joke SCP about amnestics (Seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
I was summoned by PM. Let's do this!

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

First of all, I want to clarify that humor is subjective (I laugh with almost everything), so I might not be able to tell if people will like this or not. I'll give you crit from my point of view.

A club classified as an SCP-J by the CKG Gathering due to its ability to erase memories

I think this would be the second article regarding the CKG Gathering, so there's almost nothing about CKG's lore. You may or may not expand it, but you'll need to explain some things here: Why do the CKG want to erase memories? What's the object class? What are their "protocols" for the usage of the club?

will subvert the reader's expectation by revealing the Foundation simply decided to use other tools to bash heads

You can achieve this by constantly calling them "amnestics", and then revealing a photo of an aluminium bat(And I think that would be really funny, ngl). But I'm concerned about the way you're going to write the article. Are you going to add interviews, reports, test logs…? Of course, they all would be in the 'CKG format', but I want to know what kind of layout you're going to use, especially to display the modern version of the object.

Also, while I like the idea of hitting someone in the head to erase their memory, I feel like this is a little… sour. I think you should add some kind of story to it, even a little one. Maybe they were using the same guy for all the tests and they had comedic reactions? Maybe some people used the object by accident? Maybe the CKG kept using it on each other by accident or something?

Overall, I really like this idea, but humor is very subjective, so I'll suggest reaching out to other reviewers to see their opinions.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look!

item.title: Re: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.content:encoded:
Food for thought counterpoints:

The Serpent's Hand can also be seen as an elitist, objectivist organization operating on the most dangerous interpretation of "Do what you will." They operate on the assumption that their cause is righteous and inviolable, deriding and harassing any who oppose their unquestionable judgement. No locked door can ever be justified, no matter what lies on the other side. No cage can be justified, no matter what it holds back. Knowledge is free for anyone regardless of intent, except to those deemed unworthy- especially those who question any of the previous.

The Foundation is an organization of mortals, holding back a hostile universe through grit and wit. They have no illusions about their own ethics- They know that sometimes the right call is the lesser of two evils, and accept the consequences of that. They know that simply trying to find more than those two options can have consequences, and accept those as well. They aren't the knight in shining armor. But they aren't the wicked stepmother, either. They're the woodsman with the axe, and they're here to chat with this alleged grandma about where the kid in the red jacket went.

TL;DR: If you're looking for clear good guys and bad guys in the SCPverse, you're not going to find them.

item.title: Grant Request For Anti-Fire fire
item.content:encoded:
The anomaly is a bunch of matchsticks that create an odd-colored fire. When that fire is put on regular fire, the regular fire will be burnt off by the normal fire. The explanation will be that the anomalous fire uses normal fire as fuel and burns off any approaching oxygen, thus taking down both fires

Hook : Right after the description, a heavily shortened Prometheus Labs document will be there, revealing that it was found in a closed laboratory belonging to them.

The article will explain that due to the effort it takes to take down large fires, a scientist decided that the best solution will be to create anomalous fire which can burn fire. It was originally planned to be sold to civilians in the form of matches so that they can bring it around in case of fires (Due to the slow-acting nature of this, firefighters will probably stick to water). At first, the problem section is still being written.

An audio file which is discovered in another lab will be transcribed below, recording the voice of the scientist and his boss testing out prototypes. Several problems are quickly discovered by the boss. 1. For automatic fire extinguishing, sprinklers still outclass it. 2. The anomalous fire consumes oxygen, thus meaning that it can still cause smoke and suffocation, the most dangerous parts of a fire. 3. It does nothing to stop the spread of the normal fire if it's in a big enough space, thus only reducing the size of the fire. In the end, it is revealed that due to the problems discovered, the project is canceled.

I wanted to try and write a tale of the creation of an anomalous object that in paper sounds useful yet in practice, it is noticeably terrible and why testing is extremely important.

item.title: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
Don't think of a bank account as something that has a dollar added to it or subtracted from it ad random. Think of it as a record of transactions, or a closed system of exchanges. Money does not come from nowhere - someone has to be depositing money into those accounts from business entity. This might be a neat use case for Envelope Logistics, if that's a direction you want to take it.

Basically, make sure there's some kind of reasonable path for the consumer to get money. Maybe they get diamonds or processed gold in the mail, or winning lottery tickets, etc.

item.title: Right Brained Sewing Machine.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A seemingly sapient sewing machine that is able to produce thread out of any material inserted into it. Rudimentary brain made out of millions of wires by its needle. Three knobs. One that controls the temperature inside the storage container, one that changes the settings of the machine depending on the material's hardness and another that changed how the machine sews. Third knob has 'Manual' option to manually use the machine, 'Automatic' option to create the desired outcome (input through speaking to machine) like a 3D printer and a 'Learning' option which makes the machine experiment with its own design and material used, creating some funky and inventive clothing items. Items created by the machine are not anomalous unless the material was anomalous. Can mix many types of material together. Can quickly respond to yes/no questions by using a high/low pitched beep. Responds to open-ended questions by sewing the answer together. Foundation uses this to 'interview' machine.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Incomplete origin, being investigated by Foundation. Discovered inside a Mumbai hotel room. Owners seized machine after the occupant, wealthy English woman Ollie Mae Price, went missing for more than 14 days. Owners were intrigued but could not figure out how to use the machine. Experimented with it and created a bra made of wool whilst using the automatic setting. Owners then made bras out of glass and porcelain. Began to sell the pieces on a street stall, stirring widespread rumours that ultimately reached The Foundation. Foundation questioned the owners briefly, dispensing Class B amnestics after seizing the machine. Foundation found some people from Dharavi wearing purple-dyed metallic shirts, coats and skirts. Suspicions arose that Ollie had been supplying clothes made by the machine to the Dharavian citizens for an unknown, possibly benevolent reason. Foundation now has an immense interest in the machine to efficiently create armours as well as replace lose laundry. Foundation interviews the machine to explore its origin, creator as well as the whereabouts of Ollie and what her motives were with the machine. Through continuous use of the 'learning' feature, the machine now knows how to make more complex items such as basic microchips and explosive devices. Machine uses the initals D.W when asked about who or what created them, nothing more.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The endless possibilities and uses The Foundation has with the machine, much like SCP-294. The machine's 'learning' feature establishes its own growth as an entity and how it is gaining knowledge and changing before The Foundation's eyes.

Additional Notes: If it's not Greenlight worthy yet, please send me some suggestions below! They will be very much appreciated.

item.title: The 14th
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Currently, there are 13 members of the O5 council. However, there are speculations of a possible 14th member, who's been exiled from the SCP foundation. No one knows who he is, where he came from, and what happened to him.

Central Narrative: He exists, that's for sure. Most staff know him by now, the 14th member, or O5-14. He doesn't have a specified name, age, or appearance, we just know he exists. When spoken about in front of the O5 council, they're all usually quiet, and refuse to give details. One person who seems to be connected to the 14th member is a janitor, Raphael Moore. He's dead though, maybe. No information about him, he was only a janitor who knew one of O5's biggest secrets.

What happened to the 14th member? Quite simply, he was exiled. No one knows why he was exiled. A document confirming his exile was found in a cabinet, dating back to December 16th, 1855. Most of the document was either torn off, or burnt, only the date remained.

There are 3 sections to this tale. the 14th, the meeting, and the disappearance. In the first section, it explains who he was, and when he was exiled (of course, no one knows why). In the 2nd section, it takes place in 2019, a meeting held between the O5 council, and site directors of over 100 facilities, all wondering the same thing, "Who is the 14th?". Stalemate, obviously. Final section, the disappearance… of Raphael Moore, the man connected to the 14th. The disappearance of this man lead to HUGE speculation, investigations, and concerns within the SCP foundation, causing revolts, rebellions, all the fun ingredients for disaster.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Sure, a small tale, but a rather intriguing and mysterious tale.

Additional Notes: It probably sucks.

item.title: Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Yes, but what does nostalgia have to do with Sarkicism, then? Now it's moving in a different direction of horror, which is at odds with your feelings of being calm / at ease.

Ideally, whatever you add to the concept needs to link together. So, for example, is there another entity / reason why these people are being kept in the village against their will?

e.g. Is there like the spirit of a small child who lost her parents to a fire long ago, and now casts a spell on anyone who enters so that they will never leave her again?

Have a reason for your anomaly. It doesn't have to be spelt out in the actual article, but you as the author need to know it.

item.title: Re: Try again? Fugitive vs the Yakuza
item.content:encoded:
Requested to review by Wikidot PM.

+ show block
– hide block

"You here to talk to the boss?"

Personally, I feel like this should be its own separate line.

He smiles when you arrive at his desk.

I can't place my finger on it, but this just seems out of flow for the rest of the interaction. You'd think this guy would smile on first seeing him, or as he was lighting the cigarette.

"Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette.

"So tell me, how did you get this money?" Tsuyaki blows smoke into your face as he talks.

You could probably combine this into one paragraph: "Thank you." Tsuyaki leans back in his chair, and lights a cigarette. He blows smoke into your face as he continues to talk. "So tell me, how did you get this money?"

"Really? Not many people who come to me have 10,000,000 yen. It's even stranger that a foreigner would." Tsuyaki leans forward.

"So tell me. Did you steal this money?"

Same here.

"No, I don't like having a target on my back." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

Yet more weird line breaking. I think it flows better as:

"No, I don't like having a target on my back."

"I guess that's why you want me to smuggle you off the island." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

You remain silent as you wait for your reward.

"Or are you running from the GOC?"

Probably would combine this with the paragraph above it.

Tsuyaki's eyes dart behind you for a brief moment.

Make this separate from the reader's dialogue. At this point, I think you get my drift. Keep Tsuyaki's actions separate from the reader's dialogue, and vice versa. I'm going to stop pointing it out now.

You simultaneously remove your gun, and shoot the right in the chest.

Did you accidentally a word here?

"I would never help you. Traitors deserve to die." Tsuyaki begins to laugh.

Yeah, this is some Snidely Whiplash levels of villain dialogue here, my dude. I imagine people who just had a gun fired next to their head are not quite cartoony when they speak.

When the three guards rush around the corner, you begin to open fire. one goes down, as the others duck behind cover, and return fire.

Ending two sentences after another with the same word always parses weird to me. Might want to switch up the vocab for one of these two.

The only survivors of the operation was Roach and fellow
strike team members Echo and Blanket. After review of the

Weird line break here.

All in all, it's a bit of a fun ride through the various iterations of these events. Nothing groundbreaking, but a neat bit of noir-style action. That said, when you get to the personnel file on roach you really break all your flow and momentum to a halt. To be honest, that level of exposition kills the story dead. While it is likely going to be essential info for your overall story arc, I'd say it would be better if you capped off the story and including the file in another piece. But that's just my opinion.

item.title: Re: The Phantom
item.content:encoded:
If this thing has supposedly "superior intelligence", then why not try and cut a deal with The Foundation to help its mission? It has to realize that with the resources of The Foundation backing it, it would be a lot easier to accomplish its mission, both in terms of finding suitable victims as well as providing protection on the way to its eventual goal.

The Foundation has no problems killing people if the means justify the ends; if they know that the deaths prevent a cataclysm, they would likely support the being.

Also, you need to delineate the specific cataclysm. A generic cataclysm doesn't inspire horror like a specific one does. So have some fun with it.

Lastly, give us some details on the GOI. While you can get away some generality, at least mention if it's an evil cult, some businessmen with philanthropic ideals, or even a human-sacrificing cult with philanthropic ideals. Just something would help here.

item.title: Re: New SCP. Der Verlorene
item.content:encoded:
The problem is that seems to be just a single instance of a shellshocked soldier. With that as a given, there's little of interest here. You need to build more into the character than that; if he could be treated then he may give some interesting historical notes, even possibly describe the SCP that transported him through time.

Or he could have the ability to time travel himself, and the ability was triggered due to stress. even if it was a one-time ability, it could be fascinating to study him. If it's not, then he could be of help in exploring historical eras, possibly confirming details.

If you are going to keep him shellshocked, then you need to show what he can add to the knowledge of The Foundation. There has to be some sign of what caused him to time travel or it's just a neat idea.

In what seems to be a common theme today, this is just the beginning of an idea, and needs to be fleshed out somewhat or it's just The Foundation equivalent of a freak; he's going to be confined until he dies, possibly gets killed, and not really contribute anything.

item.title: Re: The Railyard To Everywhere
item.content:encoded:
This is not a bad idea, and has a lot of great detail. However, the biggest problem is that the intelligence that set this up is not even hinted at, no trademarks, company signage, or anything like that. This sounds like something that was expensive to create and maintain, and that requires some sort of intelligence, even if it's just company of some sort.

Basically, whoever set it up needs to be defined and given some explanation here.

Also, if there needs to be some form of security. If they can't control who comes in, they can control what people do there. Even if it's just an old man with a whistle, if they are worried enough about there cargo that they are willing to kill for it, then it makes no sense to not have some form of security.

Lastly, you may want to consider who they are doing business with. There is no such thing as a stop that's just a stop; why is there a junction on Earth, and who are they doing business with here? Even if they are restocking, how are they doing that?

Good skeleton; now flesh it out.

item.title: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings about this. The core ideal is fine, but I'm morally obligated to point out that compulsion should be avoided.

The first two logs are good. The third is entirely too wordy and I think breaks the suspension of disbelief - O5 should have more control over itself and realize exactly what is happening - not break down into disorder and infighting.

The description is greatly improved but there's still a massive dangling thread in that 'bank account money' comes out of thin air, which can't really happen with such a computerized banking system we have today. I think there's room for cleverness in handling that can add verisimilitude to what is admittedly a rather wacky article. The asteroid bit is also entirely extraneous and I'm not sure what its purpose is.

The writing is certainly better than the original article, but I think I would still no vote. The logs add a lot but my opinion is soured by the third log. The ending still works as it did in the original article. As a rewrite, I think you're still a bit hamstrung by the original core idea and I'm not sure there's much that can be done to mitigate that without changing the article fundamentally.

item.title: Re: SCP-5832
item.content:encoded:
1) You don't need to make it an SCP; once it demonstrates anomalous attributes it's a given. Also, it feels that this has not been greenlighted but it already has a number.

2) The Red Paper Castle: It may be better to phrase it such that the red paper was transformed into a duplicate of the original castle. I know it's semantics, but it just feels better. You may want to go through and look for similar instances; there are a number of similarly bulky phrasing.

3) This is a good start, but it needs to be expanded upon. Do they have a history? Why did they automatically become enemies, with no apparent attempt at diplomacy? Where are they getting more paper to build the castle? If I put a pack of white paper near the castle, what would happen? Did they have a religion prior to the researcher? What form does that worship take?

Heck, what's the psychology of the castle dwellers? Is it based off real medieval people or an idealized form, such as the SCA? For that matter, why was it built in the first place, was it for a warg game or just to see what could happen?

Again, really cool start. Now flesh it out.

Forum thread: SCP-5832

Downvote for me, sorry.

The concept is good and its core, the logs, was well done. As a general narrative I have no qualms.

But I think a lot of aspects from the Foundation got lost for no reason:

1- This is not Neutralized, since it still works, it is just depressed;
2- It shouldn't be in a Standard Containment, first because it is an SCP, secondly because it is Sentient and self-motile;
3- The description cuts right to "it Anderson's, so that's why it is anomalous", giving unnecessary context without describing it or it properties in any relevant way. It sounds like a Task Force report, not the finished article;
4- A lot of details on GOIs' activities that have no bearing in the story and I don't really care;
5- They do no test whatsoever, then someone wants to use it because why not.

Let me be clear, I have nothing against the Foundation deciding to use an anomaly whose effects are actually useful and understood enough for some safety and reliability. But without tests there is no safety and reliability in it. This thing is a frigging autonomous AI, it could do horrible shit out of the blue for unknown reasons, at the very least, without some tests.

Some logs could be those tests, by the way, at least some of them. A single dummy test isn't nearly enough, and even downplaying the dumb "lets fry D-Classes for cheap data"a surgeon just begs for tests with D-Classes that needed the surgery because of accidents and stuff.

As a general concept we already have SCP-2295 and, with a different area of work, SCP-1230. So the good parts aren't enough for not downvoting.
